text: A night paid a priest to forgive a crime he hadn't committed yet.
You see, the priest was traveling from town to town selling forgiveness for coins.
Lying had a price, stealing had a price, and the worst the sin, the more you paid.
People lined up for hours to drop their money into his huge iron chest.
So, the night stepped up and asked to be forgiven for something he was planning to do next week.
The priest hesitated, charged a mixture, and stamped the paper anyway.
A few days later, the priest left town through the forest, with the chest so full it took two men to carry it.
That's where the night was waiting.
He took every last coin, and when the priest screamed that he'd go to hell for it, the night just held up the paper.
The crime he'd paid to be forgiven for was robbing the man who sold it to him.
